stories.ltme_summary: At the IBA 2026 conference, a former American bar chief said embattled US judges would be remembered as history's heroes. The Law Society Gazette reports that law firms which did not bend to Trump are thriving.

stories.title: 'Positive' steps made as small firms talk face-to-face with SRA
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that small firms have talked face-to-face with the Solicitors Regulation Authority and that the talks produced positive steps. Reforms due to take effect in January are now on hold while discussions with the regulator continue. The report is dated 12 October 2026.
stories.hook: The SRA has paused January reforms for small firms while talks with the regulator continue.

stories.title: Solicitor lied to court with backdated letter in attempted cover-up
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports on a solicitor who tried to argue he had served a claim form on the right party, after producing a backdated letter that the court found to be a cover-up attempt.

stories.title: Judges receive cautious green light for AI use
Uncertainty surrounds PM's pledge on 'non-compete' clauses
stories.ltme_summary: The Prime Minister has pledged to legislate against non-compete clauses as a drag on innovation, according to The Law Society Gazette. The government's announcement gave few details, leaving its approach uncertain.

stories.title: Plaid held talks with Burnham on justice devolution
stories.ltme_summary: The Welsh government's counsel general says talks were held with Burnham on justice devolution and that a separate Welsh jurisdiction is back on the table. The Law Society Gazette reported the remarks on 12 October.

stories.title: Remote hearings pilot to speed up justice
Conditions could be imposed on barristers awaiting misconduct hearing
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Bar regulator will be able to impose conditions on barristers awaiting misconduct hearings, a halfway point between normal practice and interim suspension.

stories.title: In depth: Jury trials back in the crosshairs
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports alarm at plans to remove a defendant's right to elect jury trial while increasing magistrates' sentencing powers. Volunteers are described as unequipped to try complex, multi-day trials.

stories.title: Ex-A&O boss co-founds AI law firm
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that a former A&O executive has co-founded an AI law firm. The venture is described as taking aim at the billable hour. The extract is brief and gives no names, dates or funding details.
stories.hook: Former A&O boss co-founds AI-driven law firm that targets the billable hour

stories.title: SRA proposes minor SQE1 syllabus tweaks despite concerns it covers too much law
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that the Solicitors Regulation Authority has launched a consultation on minor changes to the SQE1 syllabus. The story notes concern that the syllabus covers too much law. The report is dated 12 October 2026. The proposals affect future solicitor qualification candidates in England and Wales.
stories.hook: The SRA consults on minor SQE1 syllabus changes despite concerns the exam covers too much law.

stories.title: Exclusive data: Solicitor apprentices can earn up to £33k straight out of school (and that’s before bonuses!)
LB100 2026: the highs, the lows and the surprises from the data
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business says its LB100 2026 data reveals wide-ranging insight into top performing firms, covering headcount, profitability and revenue per lawyer, with year-on-year comparisons.

stories.title: Arsenal names new GC after departure of long-serving legal chief
stories.ltme_summary: Arsenal has appointed Patrick Camerer Cuss as its general counsel, promoting him from associate GC, according to Legal Business. He succeeds Svenja Geissmar, who left the club this summer after 17 years.

stories.title: High Court judge rules in favour of Pogust Goodhead in Mariana Dam dispute
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that a High Court judge ruled for PGMBM, formerly Pogust Goodhead, in a dispute over which firm represents claimants in the £36bn Mariana Dam litigation.

stories.title: When PDF-Centric FOIA Workflows Start To Break Down: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Victoria Cash of Casepoint discusses where PDF-centric FOIA workflows begin to break down, in a guest post on eDiscovery Today. The commentary covers eDiscovery best practice for public records requests.

stories.title: Ask Why BEFORE Your Law Firm Buys Another AI Tool: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today runs a best-practice piece urging law firm leaders to ask why before buying another AI tool, rather than buying because firm leaders are told to. The authors are not named in the extract. The post is opinion.
stories.hook: eDiscovery Today urges law firms to ask why before buying another AI tool.

stories.title: A Conversation with Mary Mack and Holley Robinson About EDRM 2.0: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.hook: A Nextpoint write-up of a Mary Mack and Holley Robinson talk on EDRM 2.0 is flagged by eDiscovery Today.

stories.title: Current Methods to Identify AI Content: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today highlights current methods for identifying AI-generated content, drawing on a post by Damir Kahvedžić of ProSearch. The item is commentary.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse: You May Be on It Even If You Don’t Use It: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin reports that Meta's Muse AI agent reportedly builds profiles of people in users' lives, including people who do not use Muse. The claim is reported rather than independently confirmed.

stories.title: Important Court Rulings from 2026 Regarding AI: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today summarises important 2026 court rulings on artificial intelligence and says Exterro sets out the main trends from them. The post is commentary that points readers to Exterro's analysis rather than reporting the rulings directly.
stories.hook: eDiscovery Today points to Exterro's review of 2026 court rulings on AI.

stories.title: AI-Assisted Streaming Fraud Leads to Prison for Man Who Outstreamed Taylor Swift: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today reports that Michael Smith, a North Carolina man, has been sentenced to prison over AI-assisted streaming fraud involving songs that outstreamed Taylor Swift.

stories.title: The Kitchen Sink for October 9, 2026: Legal Tech Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today publishes a weekly roundup for 9 October 2026 covering legal technology trends. Topics include monitoring of lawyers at firms and Meta's tax strategy for data centres. The post is a commentary digest rather than a single news report.
stories.hook: Doug Austin's weekly kitchen sink covers firm monitoring of lawyers and legal tech trends.

stories.title: Contrary to Law to Order the Production of the Entirety of Expert’s ChatGPT History Log, Court Rules: eDiscovery Case Law
stories.hook: Nevada court limits production of an expert's full ChatGPT history in discovery
entities: Villanueva v. Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department

stories.title: AI Coding Agents Productivity Gains Offset by Human Review: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today reports that gains from AI coding agents are being offset by human review bottlenecks. The post is commentary on AI productivity rather than a new development.

stories.title: The Worst of Us
stories.ltme_summary: Carolyn Elefant argues on MyShingle that AI has exposed existing problems in the legal profession rather than creating them. She cites a Reuters report on a Florida appellate order to show cause over a 41-page filing.

stories.title: Firms Bought the AI. Then They Benched KM.
stories.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

seen_in.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

stories.ltme_summary: Greg Lambert of 3 Geeks and a Law Blog argues that law firms bought wide AI licences, then cut knowledge management, based on his conversations with vendors and firms.

stories.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

seen_in.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

stories.ltme_summary: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog interviews Ross Guberman and Heather Rodriguez of BriefCatch about legal writing when first drafts are cheap, with the company's origins in Guberman's books and workshops.

stories.title: Help the NCSC understand how organisations approach external attack surface risk
stories.ltme_summary: The National Cyber Security Centre is asking people who evaluate, select or adopt external attack surface management (EASM) tools to share their experience. It wants to understand how organisations approach risk from external attack surfaces. The call is dated 12 October 2026. The item is a research request, not a finding.
stories.hook: The NCSC wants to hear from buyers of external attack surface management tools for a research exercise.

stories.title: Practice Direction on Listing and guidance for live links in the criminal courts comes into effect tomorrow
stories.hook: A national framework for listing criminal cases and live links guidance takes effect on 1 October 2026.

stories.title: Child defendants in the Crown Court – sixth edition
stories.ltme_summary: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary has published the sixth edition of its bench book on child defendants in the Crown Court. The guide gathers in one place the material a Crown Court judge or recorder needs on the subject. The notice is dated 30 September 2026 and concerns criminal court practice in England and Wales.
stories.hook: The Judiciary's sixth edition bench book on child defendants gives Crown Court judges one reference point.

stories.title: Modernisation of High Court structure comes into effect today
stories.ltme_summary: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary says the Business and Property Division of the High Court took effect on 1 October 2026. It brings together courts previously spread across the Chancery and King's Bench Divisions. The change restructures how commercial and property cases are allocated within the High Court in England and Wales.
stories.hook: The Judiciary says the Business and Property Division of the High Court took effect on 1 October 2026.

stories.title: Protocol for publishing judgments in Welsh and English
stories.ltme_summary: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary describes a pilot scheme testing whether judgments can be published in both Welsh and English. The pilot applies to the Administrative Court in Wales. The notice is dated 1 October 2026. The item concerns court publication practice in Wales.
stories.hook: A pilot in the Administrative Court in Wales tests publishing judgments in Welsh and English.

stories.title: President of the King’s Bench Division Dame Victoria Sharp retires from the judiciary
stories.ltme_summary: The Courts and Tribunals Judiciary reports that Dame Victoria Sharp has retired from the judiciary as President of the King's Bench Division. The notice, dated 1 October 2026, points to a longer piece on her tenure and the changes she led in the Division. The item is a judicial appointments update for England and Wales.
stories.hook: Dame Victoria Sharp retires from the judiciary after her term as President of the King's Bench Division.

stories.title: Rt Hon. Alex Norris sworn in as the new Lord Chancellor
stories.hook: Alex Norris MP is now Lord Chancellor, according to the Courts and Tribunals Judiciary.

stories.title: New President of the King’s Bench Division, Sir Mark Warby, is sworn in
stories.hook: Sir Mark Warby takes up the presidency of the King's Bench Division, the Judiciary confirms.

stories.title: Why Legal Operations Is Finally Getting Its Own Credential, And Why That’s Overdue
stories.ltme_summary: CLOC writes that it is building a formal certification for legal operations professionals, described as the Legal Operations credential. The post, dated 2 October 2026, argues the role has needed a recognised qualification for some time.
stories.hook: CLOC is building a formal certification for legal operations professionals

stories.title: Raise your hand to lead with CLOC in 2027
stories.ltme_summary: CLOC invites members to put themselves forward for leadership roles in 2027. A volunteer writes about a panel on how to join and stay on a board, drawing on a session at the recent conference. The post is dated 6 October 2026.
stories.hook: CLOC urges members to put their names forward for leadership roles in 2027

stories.title: Voices of CLOC | LaTrece Johnson
stories.ltme_summary: CLOC has launched a video series spotlighting members and volunteer leaders in legal operations. The series, dated 9 October 2026, will feature stories across the CLOC community through the year. This entry profiles LaTrece Johnson.

The AI Agent Privacy Problem: Who's Liable When Your Legal AI Shares Client Data?
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor discusses who bears liability when legal AI agents share client data. It argues that AI agents break the traditional model in which privilege runs through the attorney's conduct.

stories.title: Eleventh Circuit Opinion Signals Close Scrutiny of Appellate Procedure and Holdings
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor discusses an Eleventh Circuit opinion in docket 25-14467, arguing that the court's framing of issues on appeal may have broader consequences for litigants.

stories.ltme_summary: Ken Crutchfield comments on Kirkland & Ellis's decision to stop disclosing financial information to The American Lawyer and other media after 2026. Firm leadership said disclosures overemphasise quantitative metrics.

stories.title: Does Claim Stacking Actually Work? What State Trial Court Data Can Tell Us
stories.ltme_summary: Trellis analyses state trial court data on claim stacking in California labour and employment lawsuits. It finds that pairing intent-based claims with objective claims raises recovery odds, at a cost.

stories.title: ‘No More Than an Ordinary Copyright Case’ — 3rd Circuit Unseals Its Opinion In Thomson Reuters Case Against ROSS
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports on the Third Circuit's opinion in Thomson Reuters' copyright case against ROSS, describing it as the end of a 6.5-year dispute. The item is an aggregator commentary on the ruling.

stories.title: As AI Data Centers Expand, Legal Is Getting Pulled Into the Business Earlier
Former Davis Polk Attorney Launches Compliance Startup Leela, Announces $4.6M Seed Round
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Leela, a compliance startup founded by a former Davis Polk attorney, has announced a $4.6M seed round. According to the report, the funding will be used to hire for compliance and engineering roles and to build integrations that suit users with different technology stacks.
stories.hook: Leela, founded by an ex-Davis Polk attorney, raises a $4.6M seed round to build compliance software

stories.title: Third Circuit Opinion in No. 25-3170: What Practitioners Should Watch
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor advises practitioners to check the text and holding of the Third Circuit opinion in No. 25-3170, dated 5 October 2026, directly from the docket. The piece says the main near-term point is procedural.
